title.narrative: Provision and Strengthening of Community-Based Protection Systems for Vulnerable Women, Children, and Persons with Disabilities in Jere and Fune LGAs in Borno and Yobe States

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtCommunities in Jere and Fune LGAs continue to face persistent protection risks driven by protracted conflict, climate shocks, food insecurity, and a weakened social support environment. Women, girls, and persons with disabilities remain disproportionately exposed to GBV, exploitation, child protection violations, and barriers in accessing essential services. With overstretched community structures and reduced funding for specialized protection services, urgent and innovative solutions are required to strengthen the protective environment.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtUnder the NHF Third Standard Allocation 2025 – Thematic Envelope 2: Protection of Vulnerable Groups, Aid Initiative to Support Vulnerable and Idle People (AISVIP) proposes this project to reduce protection risks and revitalize community-based protection mechanisms through a hybrid model of innovative, community-led, and survivor-centered protection services.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThis project will focus several innovative approaches, including:ltbrgtMobile Community Protection Hubs (MCPHs): temporary, movable tents or kiosks rotating across wards to deliver integrated GBV, child protection, legal referral, PSS, and PSEAH services weekly, ensuring access for underserved and hard-to-reach areas.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtDigital Protection Alert Case Tracking System (D-PACTS): a low-bandwidth, user-friendly digital platform enabling community focal points to safely report protection concerns, track referrals, and strengthen early-warning and response mechanisms.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtCommunity Protection Micro-Initiatives (CPMIs): small-scale, community-designed protection solutions (e.g., safe lighting, girls’ peer-watch groups, disability-access ramps), supported with micro-grants and implemented directly by community protection committees.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtInclusive Protection Champions Network (IPCN): a network of trained women, youth, elders, and persons with disabilities who will lead awareness, safe referrals, and risk-reduction activities within their communities.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project will deliver comprehensive GBV and child protection services, including case management, structured psychosocial support, legal referrals, and safe spaces while integrating disability-inclusive approaches and meaningful participation of affected populations. It will also strengthen community protection committees, build capacity of frontline workers, enhance protection monitoring, and support family tracing and reunification for at-risk children.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtAligned with NHF requirements, the intervention integrates robust PSEAH systems through confidential reporting channels, capacity-building of community focal points, and engagement with the inter-agency PSEAH Network. Where required, conditional cash or voucher assistance (CVA) will be used as an innovative life-saving modality to reduce immediate protection risks such as emergency relocation, transportation, or urgent safety needs.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThrough these innovative and community-led approaches, AISVIP will contribute to a safer, more resilient Jere and Fune LGAs where women, children, and persons with disabilities have meaningful access to protection services and are empowered to reduce and mitigate long-term vulnerabilities. This fully aligns with the 2025 HNRP and NHF’s commitment to locally led, protection-centered, and innovative humanitarian response.ltbrgtlt/pgt
